question:
DRAG DROP -
Refer to the exhibit. An administrator is deploying BGP to geographically connect two data center sites. Both sites are configured for dual-stack routed protocols. The administrator must inject the IPv6 network 2001:AE4:1::/64 into the IPv6 unicast database. Drag and drop the SiteA commands from the right into the blanks in the configuration on the left. Commands are used more than once.
context: Topology: SiteA (BGP AS 65001, .1 / :1) connects to SiteB (BGP AS 65002, .2 / :2) via 172.16.10.0/24 and 2001:AE4:1::/64.
imageNote: Diagram: SiteA (BGP AS 65001, .1/:1) connects to SiteB (BGP AS 65002, .2/:2) via two links: 172.16.10.0/24 and 2001:AE4:1::/64.
theory: A dual-stack eBGP session needs a separate neighbor statement and address-family activation for each protocol: the IPv6 neighbor is activated under address-family ipv6 unicast, where the IPv6 prefix is injected with a network statement, while the existing IPv4 neighbor is activated under address-family ipv4 unicast for the IPv4 prefix. Each address family independently carries and advertises only the prefixes of its own protocol, which is why the IPv6 network statement must sit under the IPv6, not the IPv4, address family, referencing the actual /64 prefix and the neighbor's IPv6 address. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 1 — BGP Dual-Stack IPv4/IPv6 Configuration)
